tips: Add Suica to Apple/Google Wallet while on the MSP layover so you can tap through Haneda transit without stopping at a kiosk.
Hit the konbini before midnight to grab Pocari Sweat and electrolytes; jet lag and December dry cabin air will hit hard tomorrow morning.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: December evenings in Tokyo are dry but cold (often near freezing). The Shibuya Blue Cave outdoor illumination walk can be biting with wind chill off Yoyogi Park.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Shibuya Blue Cave illumination — ~600k blue LEDs toward Yoyogi
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Energy audible: if day one cooked the crew, swap Blue Cave for an early nomihodai and 23:00 lights-out — tomorrow has temples AND Akihabara.
suggestedSwap.reason: If the group is exhausted from the flight and the evening is bitterly cold, swapping the outdoor walk for an early indoor nomihodai saves energy for tomorrow's heavy outdoor temple day.

tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots are notorious for selling out; if you haven't pre-booked, pivot to Mag's Park rooftop or Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby.
Layer up for the Blue Cave walk—it's a 20+ min outdoor stroll and Tokyo evenings drop fast.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Light rain is possible in December. Senso-ji and Nakamise-dori are mostly uncovered, and Ueno Ameyoko is an open-air market.
tips: Arrive at Senso-ji before 09:00 to beat the tour bus crowds, which arrive in force by 09:30.
If the Skytree queue is insane, pivot to the Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door for the same river view with a beer in hand.

2026-12-18.crowdAlert: teamLab Planets requires strict timed entry and is extremely popular; arriving even 15 minutes late can mean denied entry.
tips: Screenshot your teamLab Planets QR codes now—spotty Wi-Fi at the venue entrance can cause panic.
Depachika (department store basement food halls) close around 20:00; hit Mitsukoshi before 18:00 for the best selection.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: High rain risk for a coastal day trip. The Enoshima island climb and Fuji-over-Sagami-Bay view are completely weather-dependent and offer zero visibility in rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay — soak with a Fuji view before the train if legs are cooked.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the outdoor climb to the Sea Candle will be miserable and the Fuji view will be obscured; swapping for the indoor onsen at Enospa saves the day with warmth and bay views.

tips: Check the Kamakura weather radar at 07:30 before heading south; if it's raining, pivot to the indoor Tokyo National Museum alt plan.
The Enoden coastal tram is charming but slow; if running behind, skip the Komachi-dori snack gauntlet and head straight to Kotoku-in.
Ghibli Museum tickets are strictly timed and non-refundable; if you have them, treat that 10:00 slot like a flight departure.
Start the Airbnb laundry during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.
When boarding the Nozomi at Tokyo Station, grab seats on the LEFT side (E seats) for the best chance at a Mt. Fuji view around minute 40.
Pontocho Alley riverside izakaya seating is highly coveted; confirm your booking for 8 promptly upon check-in.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Fushimi Inari at dawn involves a steep outdoor mountain climb. December mornings are freezing, and stone steps become slippery with frost or light rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: FUSHIMI INARI AT DAWN — the whole reason alarms exist
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Sanjusangendo — 1,001 golden Kannon statues in a 120m hall. Indoor, jaw-dropping, criminally underrated.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it's raining heavily, the Fushimi Inari climb will be a cold, slippery, photo-ruining experience; Sanjusangendo offers an incredible indoor alternative nearby.

tips: Dress in warm layers for Fushimi Inari; hand warmers (konbini purchase) are a lifesaver for the 06:45 dawn start.
Funaoka Onsen has tattoo-friendly hours; check the schedule if anyone in the group has ink.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is an outdoor walk that loses its magic in heavy rain, and the Iwatayama Monkey Park climb becomes dangerously slippery.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Iwatayama Monkey Park — humans enter the cage
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Kimono Forest at Randen Arashiyama station: pillar-lit fabric columns glowing at dusk — free, on the way out anyway.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the steep hike up to the monkey park will be too slippery and unpleasant; the covered Kimono Forest and nearby cafes offer a dry, aesthetic alternative.

tips: Wakakusa-yama is closed for the winter starting Dec 13; do NOT attempt the climb today.
Nara deer can be aggressive; buy the deer crackers, bow, and when they're gone, show empty hands to signal you're out.

2026-12-24.crowdAlert: KFC for Christmas dinner is a massive Japanese tradition; if you want the Christmas bucket, pre-order or expect 1-2 hour waits at any KFC in Osaka.
tips: Nintendo Museum lottery tickets are locked; if the whole group lost, pivot to Uji's Byodo-in and Tsuen tea for a beautiful morning.
Buy Rikuro's jiggly cheesecake near Namba station early in the day; they sell out by evening.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ on Christmas Day will be at peak capacity. Super Nintendo World timed entry is a bloodbath if you don't rope-drop immediately.
tips: If you don't have Express Passes, use the single-rider lines for Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey to save 60% of the wait.
Download the USJ app before arriving to monitor real-time wait times and secure timed-entry tickets.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima's floating torii gate is best at high tide, but December weather can bring rain and heavy winds that cancel ferries.
tips: Check the Miyajima tide times before leaving Hiroshima; low tide means the torii sits in mud, which is less photogenic.
This is the longest day of the trip; anyone redlining should skip Miyajima, do the museum unhurried, and meet at Hiroshima station.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: The Midosuji Illumination is a 4km outdoor walk; December nights in Osaka are freezing, and wind chill along the long boulevard is brutal.
tips: 551 Horai pork buns sell out nightly; grab a 4-pack from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner to secure house breakfast.
If the 4km Midosuji walk is too cold, hop between illuminated sections using the Midosuji subway line.
Himeji Castle involves a steep, strenuous climb; pace yourself before the Kobe beef lunch.
Do a tax-free paperwork check tonight: ensure receipts are stapled to passports and purchases are accessible for customs on exit.
When boarding the Nozomi east, grab seats on the LEFT side (A seats) for the final Mt. Fuji view.
Zero out your Suica card by using it for konbini runs or the Keikyu airport transit to avoid leaving yen on the card.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161.85, your dollar stretches far. Withdraw cash from 7-Eleven ATMs for the best exchange rates and avoid airport currency counters.
December in Japan is cold and dry, but rain is possible. Pack a lightweight, packable rain jacket and a warm beanie—layering is key for outdoor temple mornings and illuminated night walks.

If buying Japanese whisky (Hibiki/Yamazaki) at duty-free, buy it AFTER security at Haneda and keep it sealed. Since you have a US connection at MSP, you cannot bury it in a checked bag during transfer.
